results.title: Teaching the dot-com bubble as contrast cases
results.content: A common misconception is that the Nasdaq rose about 400% between 1995 and 2000. The figure in the source is 600%. Learners also conflate the NASDAQ Composite with the NASDAQ-100; the peak and the trough figures come from different indices. Contrast cases work well here: survivors beside casualties, and the same companies valued two ways. Teaching this as a before/after pair lands the causal point - what changed was the pricing of belief, not the technology.

results.title: Misconceptions about the crash
results.content: Another misconception is that the crash ended the internet economy, rather than repricing it. Several of the era's companies survived and grew. Avoid spending a slide on definitions; the contrast carries the takeaway in 15 seconds.
